question.text: The Aland [Oh-land]Islands, a Swedish-speaking archipelago forming an autonomous region of Finland, are found in this gulf, the northernmost arm of the Baltic Sea. This gulf separates Finland and Sweden.
question.clue: To the west of Finland is this gulf and northernmost arm of the Baltic Sea. It contains the Aland Islands and serves to separate Finland and Sweden.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about mink in history.
swap.text: In this country, 17 million minks were killed in a scandal named "minkgate" over fears that they would harbor COVID-19.
swap.clue: A queen and regent of this country was opposed by a band of pirates called the Victual Brothers during a siege against Albert of Mecklenburg.

question.text: This Northern European country had its neutrality broken when it was sold out to the Nazis by the traitor Vidkun Quisling.
question.clue: Another leader of this country served with Josef Terboven and was executed with Albert Hagelin after establishing a fascist government.

swap.leadin: The author of the Prose Edda, Snorri Sturluson, was a law speaker of a parliament in this country.
swap.text: Name this country home to the Althing, so-named to trick people to move to Greenland.
swap.clue: In 1986, Mikhail Gorbachev and Ronald Reagan met at a summit in this country's capital city that eventually resulted in the signing of the Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces Treaty.

question.leadin: He was given the epithets "The Golden King" and "The Lion of the North."
question.text: Name this Swedish king who won at the Battle of Breitenfeld and died at the Battle of Lutzen.
question.answerHtml: Gustavus Adolphus [or Gustav II Adolf; prompt on partial]
question.clue: In addition to ending the Kalmar War, one military rival to this person employed an elector named Maximilian I that died with him at Ingolstadt after losing to the numerically superior force of this ruler at the Battle of the Rain.

swap.leadin: The Treaty of Knared ended a war that shares a name with this union.
swap.text: Name this union of Scandinavia first ruled by Eric of Pomerania to counter the influence of the Hanseatic League.
swap.clue: Members of the Sture family served as regents to this state, which was targeted by the Engelbrekt rising.

question.text: Due to its ties to Poland, Saxony became embroiled in this long and destructive European conflict of the early eighteenth century. The power of Sweden began to decline after this war's Battle of Poltava.
question.answerHtml: the Great Northern War [prompt on just "Northern War"]
question.clue: During this war, one side relieved a siege during a snowstorm at the Battle of Narva.

swap.text: The Hanse became involved in political issues as well, such as the Swedish War of Liberation, in which Gustav Vasa deposed a Norwegian-Danish king of this name as regent of the Kalmar Union. That "second" king of this name had carried out the Stockholm Bloodbath.
swap.clue: After the Englebrecht Rebellion, the Swedish gained some independence before this ruler's invasion in 1520. An ally of Gustav Trolle, he perpetrated the Stockholm Bloodbath. In karmic retaliation, Frederick I imprisoned this man for 27 years.

question.leadin: This scientist claimed he "lived like a sage and died like a fool" after he refused to use the restroom at a banquet and died of a bladder or kidney condition.
question.text: Name this scientist who constructed the Uraniborg observatory as Lord of Hven. He wore a brass nose after losing a duel.
question.clue: This Danish scientist and author of Introduction to the New Astronomy died after contracting a kidney ailment that was brought on by a banquet in which he refused to leave the table to relieve himself so as to avoid committing a social faux pas.

swap.leadin: He was promoted to colonel for bravery at Mukden, and joined with Ernst Linden to win victory for the White Guards in his country's Civil War.
swap.text: Name this man who was again called up to defend his country during the Continuation War.
swap.clue: Thor Damen recorded several minutes of a private conversation between this man and Hitler when Hitler visited him for his seventy-fifth birthday.

question.text: After he crowned Joseph as king, Bonaparte came to support a French marshal of this house to succeed the childless Charles XIII. This house rules Sweden today.
question.clue: The founder of this dynasty was once implicated in the Rennes Plot, and became the governor of Hanover and Bremen before being awarded the title of Prince of Pontecorvo.

swap.leadin: Christer Pettersen was convicted but later acquitted of this man's murder.
swap.text: Name this politician from the Social Democratic Party, a prime minister of Sweden who was killed in 1986 while walking home from the cinema with his wife.
swap.clue: This politician from the Social Democratic Party, a prime minister of Sweden who was killed in 1986 while walking home from the cinema with his wife

question.text: The Kalmar Union was founded by this monarch, who ordered that the False Olaf be burned with a necklace of his forged letters as kindling. The Victual Brothers were employed against this "Semiramis of the North" during her siege of Stockholm.
question.answerHtml: Margaret I of Denmark [accept Margaret Valdemarsdotter; prompt on Margaret]
question.clue: This ruler, who was often mocked as being "Pantsless" by Albert of Mecklenburg, was the first target of the Victual Brothers, who provided supplies to counteract this ruler's siege of Stockholm.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about emigration from the Eastern Bloc.
swap.text: A series of 1975 accords signed in this country's capital eased Eastern Bloc immigration policies during a detente in US-Soviet relations. This country continued a policy of "active neutrality" under Urho Kekkonen.
swap.answerHtml: Finland [or Suomi; or Republic of Finland or Suomen tasavalta or Republiken Finland] (The accords were the Helsinki Accords.)
swap.clue: The Grand Duchy of this modern day country was established shortly after the Diet of Porvoo.

question.text: This king baptized Leif Ericson and was instrumental in the spread of Christianity throughout Norway, building its first Christian church. In his attempts to make Sweden Christian as well, he offered marriage to the pagan Sigrid the Haughty.

swap.leadin: This man became the highest-profile person to be executed in a "legal purge" in his country after World War II.
swap.text: Name this politician who overthrew Haakon VII to take power in 1940.
swap.clue: This politician launched their political career in a series of articles explaining their 'political thoughts' on the death of mentor Fritjohf Nansen.

question.text: In this early battle of the Winter War, Russian troops on the Raate and Juntusranta roads were easy prey for defenders under Colonel Hjalmar Siilasvuo. Of the 44,000 in the Russian 44th, only 5,000 made it back to Russia.
question.clue: The earlier Winter War saw the Finns decisively beat the Russians nearby the Gulf of Bothnia at this battle. Hjalmar Sililasvuo led Finnish forces here, defeating General Alexey Vinogradov and General Ivan Dashitsev.

swap.text: The strike led this theater director, divorced single mother, and breast cancer survivor to run for President of Iceland; she served as the first elected woman head of state from 1980 to 1996. Please give her first name.

question.text: The Finnish-German alliance did not stay intact, and in this 1944-45 war, Germany decided to secure Petsamo while their 20th Mountain Army got consistently owned in the namesake geographical region.
question.clue: After signing an armistice with the Soviet Union in 1944, Finland fought this war in order to expel German troops from its territory.

swap.leadin: This term arose in West Germany in reference to the Soviet influence over its neighbors.
swap.text: Name this process where a large power gradually acquires cultural and political influence over a smaller one, as the USSR did to a Scandinavian state during the Cold War.
swap.clue: This term describing the domination of the politics of a small country by a larger neighbor. It originally referred to relations between the Soviet Union and the country it once fought in the Winter War.
